title.description: The dish's name, for the report.

file.description: Where the recipe is written. Carried for the caller; the solver ignores it.

portions.description: How many plates the recipe makes in all. It must cover every meal that eats it, for every person. Plates left over are reported as spare.

cooks.description: How many times it is cooked. 1, the default, for a batch cooked once. A dish made fresh each time has one cook for each meal that eats it. Must divide portions.

anchor.description: The name of the main ingredient. Every other ingredient with a book amount stays in proportion to it. Needed when any ingredient has a book amount.

max_batch_g.description: The most food, in grams, that one cook may hold: the pot's limit.

ingredients.description: What goes into it. Leave out for a frozen recipe.

name.description: The ingredient's name, as the nutrition table has it.

unit.description: The unit its amounts are in: g, ml, tsp, tbsp and so on. Leave out, or write each, for a counted item such as an egg.

note.description: Picks a second set of values in the nutrition table: rice with the note "dry weight" uses the row named rice|dry.

book.description: The amount the source recipe uses. With it, the ingredient follows the anchor. Without it, the ingredient is sized freely between min and max.

min.description: The least of it to use. Needed, with max, for the anchor and for any ingredient without a book amount.

max.description: The most of it to use.

step.description: The smallest sensible change in its amount: 10 for 10g of meat, 1 for an egg. Left out, it is 5 for g and ml, 0.25 for tsp, 0.5 for tbsp, and 1 for anything else.

role.description: Which band it may move in: a key of the targets' ratio_bounds, such as veg, liquid, fat, salty or fixed. Left out, it is default. Only with a book amount.

lo.description: Replaces the low end of its role's band, as a multiple of its book ratio to the anchor. Only with a book amount.

hi.description: Replaces the high end of its role's band. Only with a book amount.

per_portion.description: True when min and max are for one plate, not one cook: a side, or something made to order. Not with a book amount.

portions.description: Portions of veg and fruit, towards five a day.

frozen.description: Set this, and no ingredients, for plates taken from the freezer. Nothing is cooked or bought for them.

recipes.description: The recipes to scale, each under an id of your choosing. Days name recipes by these ids.

days.description: The days to plan, in order.

day.description: The day's name, such as Mon 2026-11-09.

meals.description: The recipe ids each meal eats, under the meal's name. The meals are the ones the targets' meal_kcal names, and a day needs every one. A recipe named twice is eaten twice.

people.description: How many people each meal feeds. Left out, it is 2.

carbs.description: Carbohydrate, in grams. Left out, carbs are not held to a target.

targets_per_person_day.description: What one person should eat in a day.

kcal_pct.description: How far a day's calories may be from the target, as a percentage either way.

protein_below_g.description: How many grams under its protein target a day may be.

fat_over_g.description: How many grams over its fat target a day may be.

tolerances.description: How far a day may miss a target and still pass its check.

salt_max_g_per_person_day.description: The most salt one person may eat in a day, in grams.

meal_kcal.description: Each meal's name, with the fewest and the most calories it may have as [fewest, most]. These names are the meals a day has.

carbs.description: For missing the carbs. Needed when carbs have a target.

stay_near_book.description: For an ingredient drifting from its amount in the source recipe.

weights.description: How much it costs to miss each target. A bigger number is held to more tightly.

ratio_bounds.description: For each ingredient role, how far an ingredient may move from its book ratio to the anchor, as [lowest, highest] multiples. Must have default. The roles fat and salty never go above the book, whatever their band says.

fibre_min_g_per_person_day.description: The least fibre one person should eat in a day, in grams.

min_per_day.description: The fewest portions one person should eat in a day.

pulse.description: Beans and lentils. They count once a day at most, however much is eaten.

juice.description: Juice, in grams. It counts once a day at most.

portion_g.description: What one portion of each kind weighs, in grams.

five_a_day.description: Portions of veg and fruit: how many a day, and what a portion weighs.

targets.description: What each day should come to, and how far a recipe may drift from its source.
